title: Placement and gap-finding are different diagnostics
statement: Treat placement and gap-finding as different diagnostics: placement in an ordered course needs only a short binary search, while finding gaps needs sampling across the course.
example: A binary search finds the starting unit of a 9-unit course in 3-4 items.
detail: A diagnostic BrainLift written around AP courses, one of the assessment BrainLifts given to the reading course plans, separates placement, a search for one cut-point on a roughly ordered course, from hole-filling, which assumes no order and needs the full knowledge-mapping machinery at 40-60+ items and 15-30 minutes (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/feedback/feedback3/WF - Assessment  Feedback Brain - 260624-200115.md`). For a 9-unit course the search takes 3-4 items (log₂(9) ≈ 3.2). For gaps it advises finding one, sizing it, filling it and repeating, instead of mapping every hole at once.
against: The same BrainLift rules the search out for a course with no sequential structure, which goes straight to full knowledge-mapping, and it sizes a placement two ways: 10-15 items and 5 minutes in one place, 7-10 items and 3-5 minutes in another.

evidence.quote: A placement diagnostic can be done in 10-15 items and 5 minutes.
This typically takes 3-4 items for a 9-unit course (log₂(9) ≈ 3.2).
**Insight 6: You don't need to find all the holes at once — find a hole, size it, fill it, repeat.**
Total items: typically 7-10 items. Total time: 3-5 minutes.
If the course genuinely lacks sequential structure (e.g., a collection of independent topics with no progression), this diagnostic is inappropriate — go straight to full knowledge-mapping.
